Good to know before you go

Less guessing.
More paddling.

Your first creek day? Start here.

Read all official rules ↗
Do I need a reservation?

During the operating season, walk-ins are welcome. For groups of 15 or more, call ahead to arrange your outing. Trips depend on daily conditions and availability.

Can children come along?

The minimum age is 6. Ages 6–15 must be accompanied by an adult; ages 16–17 need a parent or legal guardian to complete their waiver. Large groups have additional age and supervision requirements—contact the livery.

What should I bring?

Bring a valid photo ID to leave as a deposit, shoes that can get wet, drinking water, sunscreen, and a change of clothes. Use a proper dry bag for your phone and leave valuables at home.

What time do we need to arrive?

Upper, 9 Mile, and Full Day trips list a 10:30 am arrival deadline. Lower trips are offered before 2 pm, and Sampler trips until 3:30 pm. Confirm seasonal hours and availability before leaving.

Can I bring my own canoe or kayak?

Yes. The current site lists private-boater passes at $35 per person, plus $5 on weekends and holidays. Check in and complete waivers before launching. Boats are stacked for transport; contact staff about equipment suitability.

Are pets, alcohol, and coolers allowed?

The official rules do not allow pets on river trips and specify a non-alcohol policy. Small coolers no larger than 11 × 14 inches are allowed; glass and Styrofoam are prohibited. Read the official rules for the complete policy.

What happens if the weather or water changes?

Operations and trip options depend on weather and water conditions. Call the livery before visiting. The USGS link provides gauge readings; it is not confirmation that trips are operating.

Do you offer season passes or group rates?

The current site lists rental season passes at $240 and private-boater season passes at $180. Qualifying corporate and nonprofit groups may receive weekday discounts. Contact staff for eligibility, purchasing, and current pricing.

Rooted in the Darby

Real places.
Good people.
Great creek days.

Trapper John’s Canoe Livery operates on Big Darby Creek in Grove City, Ohio. The current website describes a history of five decades on this scenic waterway.

The experience is grounded in simple things: time outside, helpful staff, maintained equipment, and respect for the creek that makes it all possible.
